causes.label: Type of detergent
remedies: Switch to a lower sudsing detergent brand and follow instructions on package.

causes.label: Very soft water
remedies: Try less detergent.

causes.label: Too much detergent
remedies: Measure your detergent carefully.
Use less soap if you have soft water, a smaller load or a lightly soiled load.

causes.label: Fill hoses or drain hose is improperly connected
remedies: Make sure hose connections are tight at faucets and the washing machine.
Make sure the end of the drain hose is correctly inserted in and secured to the drain.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 14: "Fill hoses or drain hose is improperly connected"

causes.label: Household drain may be clogged
remedies: Check household plumbing.
You may need to call a plumber.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 14: "Household drain may be clogged"

causes.label: Constant water pressure to the fill hoses at the water source
remedies: Tighten hoses at the faucets and turn the water off after each use.
Check condition of the fill hoses; they may need replacement after 5 years.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 14: "Constant water pressure to the fill hoses at the water source"

causes.label: Using too much detergent in washer
remedies: Use less detergent.
Use less soap if you have soft water, a smaller load or a lightly soiled load.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 14: "Using too much detergent in washer"

causes.label: Cooler water temperatures provide improved energy efficiency
remedies: New laundry detergents have been formulated to work with cooler water temperatures without affecting wash performance.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 14: "Cooler water temperatures provide improved energy efficiency"

causes.label: Control is not set properly
remedies: Check water temperature control and adjust.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 14: "Control is not set properly"

causes.label: Water supply is turned off or improperly connected
remedies: Turn both hot and cold faucets fully on and make sure hoses are connected to correct faucets.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 14: "Water supply is turned off or improperly connected"

causes.label: Water valve screens are stopped up
remedies: Turn off the water source and remove the water connection hoses from the upper back of the washer.
Remove screens and use a brush or toothpick to clean the screens in the machine.
Reinstall screens, reconnect the hoses and turn the water back on.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 14: "Water valve screens are stopped up"

causes.label: House water heater is not set properly
remedies: Make sure house water heater is delivering water at 120°F–140°F (48°C–60°C).
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 14: "House water heater is not set properly"

causes.label: Drain hose is kinked or improperly connected
remedies: Straighten drain hose and make sure washer is not sitting on it.
Top of drain outlet should be less than 72″ (183 cm) above floor.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 14: "Drain hose is kinked or improperly connected"

symptoms.symptom: Water fills and drains at the same time

causes.label: Drain standpipe is too low
remedies: Drain standpipe must be above 39″ (99 cm).
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 14: "Drain standpipe is too low"

causes.label: Washer is uneven
remedies: Level the washer.
See Level the Washer.

causes.label: Washer load is unbalanced
remedies: Press the START/OFF button to stop the washer, open the lid and redistribute the load evenly.
Close the lid and restart.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 16: "Washer load is unbalanced"

causes.label: Washer is sitting too close to wall (causes knocking during cycle)
remedies: Pull washer away from the wall; about 4″ is needed.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 16: "Washer is sitting too close to wall (causes knocking during cycle)"
